* 12. applyInheritancePreview
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: editor/applyInheritancePreview
:FILE: resources/packages/app/editor/editor-inheritance-api.js
:LINE: 45
:MINS: 1.4
:END:

Inheritance changes use an authoritative preview followed by one atomic apply. The browser confirms the exact orphan binding IDs and echoes the snapshot digest; a stale request never silently accepts a refreshed deletion set. Parent-edge variation creates a sibling source and reparents the target, preserving its own composition. All consumers of that target in the branch see the change; the original source stays unchanged. The graph partial owns availability and scope wording. See [[file:../../../docs/tutorial/07-optional-required-sealed.md][lesson 7]].

:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: editor/export-plan
:FILE: src/graphden/executor/browser_plan.clj

The ordinary account menu and function picker use bundled graph plans for their local state or markup. This exporter resolves inheritance, bindings, and renames on the server and emits an ID-based plan for supported primitives; the browser does not resolve graph names itself. Shipped plans are generated during development. The generic editable-graph export takes a whole snapshot and remains unavailable under tenancy. Personal components instead use ~graphden.editor.components/export-current~, which authorizes every source dependency and exports only a bounded component plan. See the [[file:../../../resources/packages/app/ui-preview/README.md][graph-backed UI contract]].

:PROPERTIES:

:LINE: 531
:MINS: 2.6

Follow a user saving a literal input: this writer targets its function and slot, creating an own binding with POST or updating an existing one with PUT. ~authMutate~ sends the form body through ~authFetch~; ~editor-branch-context.js~ attaches the current branch to API requests. The public handler is composed in [[file:../../../resources/packages/web/crud-write/fns.edn][web/crud-write/fns.edn]]: parse, reject unsafe changes, apply the write, then invalidate and notify. Versioned storage records the change in that branch. Ordinary type diagnostics can accompany a successful save; structural or secret-flow violations reject it. The caller reloads rows and lookups, then layout and rendering show the new value. Use the reading route in [[file:../../../docs/devtour/README.md][setup]] to follow the whole round trip.

* 20. submitExecution
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: editor/submitExecution
:FILE: resources/packages/app/editor/editor-execute.js
:LINE: 291
:MINS: 6.5
:END:

The selected card's Run button delegates to the existing Inspector Run owner; it does not create another execution form. That form resolves typed inputs, keeps [[file:glossary.org::#term/effect][effect acknowledgement]] visible, and submits through this shared function. History, Trace path and Capture values are independent request options. Capture values requires tracing and explicit cost consent; cancelling consent clears that option. The submitted function UUID and generation identify this run. A new submission stops the previous poll, clears its result identity and ignores late replies; changing selection cannot relabel an earlier run. Pending runs use the same result host and cancellation path. Server execution checks remain authoritative.

- source :: [[file:../../../resources/packages/app/editor/editor-execute.js::async function submitExecution(fnEntity, args, persist, trace, captureValues,][resources/packages/app/editor/editor-execute.js:291]]

* 21. aggregatePathTrace
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: editor/aggregatePathTrace
:FILE: resources/packages/app/editor/editor-path-view.js
:LINE: 53
:MINS: 2.9
:END:

Groups a trace's invocations by function UUID, keeping call counts, cache hits and timings. Trace path without Capture values records execution without return values. With capture enabled, the latest fresh invocation owns the displayed value, including null or false. A later invocation without a value clears an earlier capture; when its capture exceeded the budget, the badge explains that the value is unavailable. It never substitutes an older result or promises to recover data that was not captured. A shortened inline preview of an available value opens the complete captured value with keyboard access. The shared popover lifecycle provides Close, bounded placement, focus return and cleanup when its anchor disappears. Secret entries carry no value.

- source :: [[file:../../../resources/packages/app/editor/editor-path-view.js::function aggregatePathTrace(entries) {][resources/packages/app/editor/editor-path-view.js:53]]

* 23. evaluate
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: editor/evaluate
:FILE: src/graphden/editor/theme.clj
:LINE: 182
:MINS: 1.7
:END:

Evaluates a selected personal theme graph in the request's existing organisation and branch. It uses the normal execution access checks, requires a non-secret pure graph, permits no effects, and limits execution to 750 ms. Only a validated theme payload reaches CSS; source graphs and execution traces are not returned. This server path is independent of the bundled local menu and picker plans. ~editor-theme-graph.js~ applies successful results and keeps saved colors when evaluation is unavailable.

Rebuilds the manifest, the fixed list of proposed objects and UUIDs, while holding the graph writer lock. It rejects a changed user, branch, source snapshot or existing identity. One transaction through the existing [[file:glossary.org::#term/protocol][storage decorators]] creates all rows with ordinary access checks. Cache-publication warnings preserve a successful commit and its identities. An internal preview lets lesson cleanup record exact new UUIDs before sending APPLY, so a lost network reply does not leave untracked objects.

Records a successful lesson installation using the returned pin, branch, package-version, content hash, and newly created namespace identities. Cleanup removes only resources attributed to this lesson. Existing namespaces and installations remain untouched; a missing or mismatched response cannot establish ownership.

:MINS: 1.9

An Apps form is an ordinary server mutation, not a tutorial-only endpoint. Before the request, the lesson saves a proposed create-only UUID and the exact handler and label. The returned receipt must match that UUID and the current organization's authoritative app list before the step completes. A missing response stays pending; a definite rejection grants no ownership. Both cleanup paths remove this exact route before its handler or branch, and retain the entire journal if removal cannot be confirmed.

* 35. _tourStartPositioning
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: editor/_tourStartPositioning
:FILE: resources/packages/app/editor/editor-tour-spot.js
:LINE: 28
:MINS: 5.1
:END:

Follows the lesson's current DOM target independently of the 600 ms completion poll. DOM, size, scroll and viewport changes coalesce into one requestAnimationFrame update; short finite CSS motion and native Web Animations reported by their owners keep updates running while active. Native motion must affect a declared step target; pause, cancellation or detachment ends frame following. The observer excludes the tour's own overlay writes, so a stationary lesson performs no geometry scans. Pause, Lessons, lesson end and teardown call ~_tourStopFollowing~ to release observers, event handlers, the viewport subscription and any queued frame.

- source :: [[file:../../../resources/packages/app/editor/editor-tour-spot.js::function _tourStartPositioning() {][resources/packages/app/editor/editor-tour-spot.js:28]]
